Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race, group, sex, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, compatible and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e

What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death occurring during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions.

Letter f

What is meant by "child survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "child growth and development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

Letter g

What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their views in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters affecting their lives.

Letter h

What is meant by "transparency" is that in the provision of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among integrated service providers.

Letter i

What is meant by "integration" is that in the provision of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is implemented by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistants, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Letter j

What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced.

Letter k

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is any action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Letter l

What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the right of victims to determine the best choice in resolving their problems.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race and group in the life of society, nation and state.

To realize the achievement of enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children as set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children both in the form of policies applicable at both national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations as well as conflict. Acts of violence against women and children constitute actions that violate, hinder, negate and disregard the human rights of women and the rights of children.

Article 20

All activities related to the organization of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children are charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget as well as other legitimate and non-binding revenues.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sukoharjo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sukoharjo.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Implementation is the form of implementing protection for women, men and child victims of violence.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

10.Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the relevant SKPD.

11.Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological, to the victim.

12.Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment based on gender and aimed at reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.

13.Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.

14.Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

15.Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

16.Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.

17.Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.

18.Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

19.Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

20.Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.

21.Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.

22.Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.

23.Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.

24.Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims in accordance with established operational standards.

25.Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

In organizing protection for victims of gender-based violence and children victims of violence, the Regional Government is assisted by Integrated Services.

Article 23

This Regional Regulation shall come into effect on the date of promulgation.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race and group in the life of society, nation and state.

To realize the achievement of enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children as set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children both in the form of policies applicable at both national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations as well as conflict. Acts of violence against women and children constitute actions that violate, hinder, negate and disregard the human rights of women and the rights of children.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race and group in the life of society, nation and state.

To realize the achievement of enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children as set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children both in the form of policies applicable at both national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations as well as conflict. Acts of violence against women and children constitute actions that violate, hinder, negate and disregard the human rights of women and the rights of children.

Article 7

(1) Integrated services as referred to in Article 6 are established by the Regional Government in accordance with statutory regulations.

(2) The establishment of integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of members from regional government elements, non-governmental institutions, health service institutions, law enforcement officers, professional workers, companion volunteers, social workers, religious counselors, safe houses (shelters), and social rehabilitation centers.

(3) Minimum Service Operational Standards for Integrated Services as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sukoharjo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sukoharjo.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Implementation is the form of implementing protection for women, men and child victims of violence.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

10.Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the relevant SKPD.

11.Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological, to the victim.

12.Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment based on gender and aimed at reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.

13.Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.

14.Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

15.Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

16.Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.

17.Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.

18.Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

19.Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

20.Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.

21.Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.

22.Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.

23.Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.

24.Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims in accordance with established operational standards.

25.Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race, group, sex, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, compatible and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e

What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death occurring during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions.

Letter f

What is meant by "child survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "child growth and development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

Letter g

What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their views in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters affecting their lives.

Letter h

What is meant by "transparency" is that in the provision of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among integrated service providers.

Letter i

What is meant by "integration" is that in the provision of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is implemented by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistants, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Letter j

What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced.

Letter k

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is any action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Letter l

What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the right of victims to determine the best choice in resolving their problems.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race and group in the life of society, nation and state.

To realize the achievement of enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children as set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children both in the form of policies applicable at both national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations as well as conflict. Acts of violence against women and children constitute actions that violate, hinder, negate and disregard the human rights of women and the rights of children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 7

(1) Integrated services as referred to in Article 6 are established by the Regional Government in accordance with statutory regulations.

(2) The establishment of integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of members from regional government elements, non-governmental institutions, health service institutions, law enforcement officers, professional workers, companion volunteers, social workers, religious counselors, safe houses (shelters), and social rehabilitation centers.

(3) Minimum Service Operational Standards for Integrated Services as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 19

(1) Control, guidance and supervision of the organization of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children is carried out by the Regent.

(2) Implementation of control, guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) on a daily basis is carried out by the relevant SKPD.

CHAPTER III

Article 20

All activities related to the organization of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children are charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget as well as other legitimate and non-binding revenues.

3.8.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sukoharjo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sukoharjo.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Implementation is the form of implementing protection for women, men and child victims of violence.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

10.Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the relevant SKPD.

11.Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological, to the victim.

12.Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment based on gender and aimed at reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.

13.Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.

14.Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

15.Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

16.Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.

17.Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.

18.Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

19.Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

20.Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.

21.Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.

22.Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.

23.Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.

24.Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims in accordance with established operational standards.

25.Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

Article 18

Assistance is carried out by persons or institutions that have expertise in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence and have cooperated with Integrated Services.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race, group, sex, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, compatible and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e

What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death occurring during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions.

Letter f

What is meant by "child survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "child growth and development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

Letter g

What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their views in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters affecting their lives.

Letter h

What is meant by "transparency" is that in the provision of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among integrated service providers.

Letter i

What is meant by "integration" is that in the provision of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is implemented by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistants, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Letter j

What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced.

Letter k

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is any action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Letter l

What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the right of victims to determine the best choice in resolving their problems.

Article 7

(1) Integrated services as referred to in Article 6 are established by the Regional Government in accordance with statutory regulations.

(2) The establishment of integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of members from regional government elements, non-governmental institutions, health service institutions, law enforcement officers, professional workers, companion volunteers, social workers, religious counselors, safe houses (shelters), and social rehabilitation centers.

(3) Minimum Service Operational Standards for Integrated Services as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race and group in the life of society, nation and state.

To realize the achievement of enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children as set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children both in the form of policies applicable at both national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations as well as conflict. Acts of violence against women and children constitute actions that violate, hinder, negate and disregard the human rights of women and the rights of children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sukoharjo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sukoharjo.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Implementation is the form of implementing protection for women, men and child victims of violence.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

10.Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the relevant SKPD.

11.Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological, to the victim.

12.Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment based on gender and aimed at reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.

13.Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.

14.Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

15.Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

16.Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.

17.Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.

18.Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

19.Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

20.Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.

21.Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.

22.Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.

23.Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.

24.Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims in accordance with established operational standards.

25.Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

Article 20

25.Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sukoharjo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sukoharjo.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Implementation is the form of implementing protection for women, men and child victims of violence.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

10.Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the relevant SKPD.

11.Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological, to the victim.

12.Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment based on gender and aimed at reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.

13.Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.

14.Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

15.Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

16.Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.

17.Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.

18.Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

19.Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

20.Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.

21.Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.

22.Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.

23.Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.

24.Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims in accordance with established operational standards.

25.Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

Article 23

This Regional Regulation shall come into effect on the date of promulgation.

I. GENERAL.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race and group in the life of society, nation and state.

To realize the achievement of enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children as set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children both in the form of policies applicable at both national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations as well as conflict. Acts of violence against women and children constitute actions that violate, hinder, negate and disregard the human rights of women and the rights of children.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sukoharjo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sukoharjo.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Implementation is the form of implementing protection for women, men and child victims of violence.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

10.Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the relevant SKPD.

11.Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological, to the victim.

12.Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment based on gender and aimed at reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.

13.Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.

14.Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

15.Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

16.Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.

17.Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.

18.Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

19.Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

20.Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.

21.Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.

22.Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.

23.Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.

24.Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims in accordance with established operational standards.

25.Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race and group in the life of society, nation and state.

To realize the achievement of enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children as set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children both in the form of policies applicable at both national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations as well as conflict. Acts of violence against women and children constitute actions that violate, hinder, negate and disregard the human rights of women and the rights of children.

2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sukoharjo.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Implementation is the form of implementing protection for women, men and child victims of violence.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

10.Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the relevant SKPD.

11.Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological, to the victim.

12.Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment based on gender and aimed at reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.

13.Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.

14.Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

15.Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

16.Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.

17.Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.

18.Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

19.Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

20.Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.

21.Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.

22.Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.

23.Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.

24.Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims in accordance with established operational standards.

25.Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race and group in the life of society, nation and state.

To realize the achievement of enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children as set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children both in the form of policies applicable at both national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations as well as conflict. Acts of violence against women and children constitute actions that violate, hinder, negate and disregard the human rights of women and the rights of children.

15.Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

16.Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.

17.Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.

18.Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

19.Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

20.Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.

21.Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.

22.Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.

23.Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.

24.Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims in accordance with established operational standards.

25.Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race and group in the life of society, nation and state.

To realize the achievement of enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children as set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children both in the form of policies applicable at both national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations as well as conflict. Acts of violence against women and children constitute actions that violate, hinder, negate and disregard the human rights of women and the rights of children.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sukoharjo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sukoharjo.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Implementation is the form of implementing protection for women, men and child victims of violence.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

10.Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the relevant SKPD.

11.Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological, to the victim.

12.Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment based on gender and aimed at reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.

13.Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.

14.Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

15.Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

16.Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.

17.Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.

18.Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

19.Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

20.Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.

21.Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.

22.Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.

23.Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.

24.Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims in accordance with established operational standards.

25.Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

Letter g

What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their views in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters affecting their lives.

Letter h

What is meant by "transparency" is that in the provision of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among integrated service providers.

Letter i

What is meant by "integration" is that in the provision of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is implemented by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistants, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Letter j

What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced.

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is any action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

I. GENERAL.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race and group in the life of society, nation and state.

To realize the achievement of enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children as set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children both in the form of policies applicable at both national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations as well as conflict. Acts of violence against women and children constitute actions that violate, hinder, negate and disregard the human rights of women and the rights of children.

I. GENERAL.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinction as to ethnicity, religion, race and group in the life of society, nation and state.

To realize the achievement of enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children as set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.

The government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children both in the form of policies applicable at both national and regional levels.

Acts of violence against women and children can occur in the public sphere as well as in the domestic sphere (within the household) and can occur at any time, in peaceful situations as well as conflict. Acts of violence against women and children constitute actions that violate, hinder, negate and disregard the human rights of women and the rights of children.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sukoharjo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sukoharjo.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Implementation is the form of implementing protection for women, men and child victims of violence.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

10.Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the relevant SKPD.

11.Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological, to the victim.

12.Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment based on gender and aimed at reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.

13.Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.

14.Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

15.Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

16.Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.

17.Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.

18.Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

19.Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

20.Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.

21.Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.

22.Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.

23.Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.

24.Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims in accordance with established operational standards.

25.Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Implementation is the form of implementing protection for women, men and child victims of violence.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

10.Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the relevant SKPD.

11.Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological, to the victim.

12.Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment based on gender and aimed at reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.

13.Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.

14.Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

15.Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

16.Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.

17.Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance.

18.Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

19.Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the household and community.

20.Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.

21.Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.

22.Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.

23.Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.

24.Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims in accordance with established operational standards.

25.Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.
